Don't reply to it at all. Real bank security never asks for your PIN — by text, email, or phone — so any reply just confirms your number is live and marks you as an easy target.

If you want something to say if you ever must answer, keep it content-free:

> "I won't share a PIN. I'll call the bank on the number on my card."

Then actually do that: hang up / stop replying, and if you're worried, ring the number printed on your card and ask them to check for anything odd on the account. Don't use any number or link the message gives you. You can also report it as spam and block the sender.
